From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Aurelia Health — post-demo: perf gating, regional routing & data jurisdiction

Hi Tim / Samantha,

Thanks again for taking the time today — good discussion and a helpful walkthrough of the expected traffic patterns. Per our ask, I wanted to capture a concise list of follow-ups so we can size a POC and confirm the right serving mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private).

Top items we need to qualify from your side:
- P95 latency SLO (end-to-end target as seen by client). Any hard limits?
- Expected peak QPS / average QPS and anticipated daily traffic window (UTC).
- Concurrency for streaming sessions (number of concurrent open streams; approximate average message length & token counts if available).
- Regional routing preferences: does traffic have to be pinned to region, are fallbacks allowed, and which regions must be strictly resident?
- Data residency constraints for PHI or regulated records (EU-only, etc.) and any logging/retention limits.
- Network egress / IP ranges or egress firewall requirements for our perf tests.

I attached an initial perf matrix (aurelia-performance-matrix-20270503.xlsx) with fields we usually need; if you can fill in the bold items it will let us pick the most cost-efficient configuration and propose a short perf test.

Proposed next steps from us:
1) You provide the short answers above + attach any sample traffic profile (CSV) — we'll map to token/byte estimates.
2) We propose a 72-hour perf test (non-prod) with controlled load, streaming checks, and regional routing enabled per your guidance.
3) Quick follow-up call to review results and scope Dedicated/Private options if needed.

Thanks — cc'ing Aditya (inference infra) and Neha (security) who will be involved on the POC and residency controls.

Best,

Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

> Hi Lauren,
>
> Great recap — answers below inline. I've attached our egress ranges as a CSV (aurelia-network-egress.csv).
>
> - P95 target: 150ms end-to-end is our preferred target for interactive experiences. We can tolerate up to 250ms for async batch-style requests.
> - Throughput: Peak expected is ~500 QPS (short bursts up to 700 QPS for 10-20s), average ~120 QPS. Traffic diurnal peak between 13:00-15:00 UTC.
> - Streaming: We expect ~80 concurrent streaming sessions at peak. Typical stream length 20-40 messages; average request payload ~1.2 KB (~150 tokens), max ~5 KB (~700 tokens).
> - Regional routing / residency: EU must be resident in EU for any PHI; APAC should stay in APAC for latency-sensitive traffic but non-PHI may be routed to US as fallback.
> - Logging: We cannot export raw request/response payloads outside the region for PHI — structured telemetry (metrics/traces) is OK if PII is redacted.
>
> Timeline: we'd like to run a POC within the next 6 weeks. Happy to start with your Hosted or Dedicated POC; if residency is strict we may evaluate Redwood Private.
>
> Cheers,

Tim — thanks for the quick turnaround and the egress file. A few proposals and clarifying questions so we can size the POC and propose a recommended configuration:

1) Serving mode recommendation (early):
   - If EU-residency for PHI is required and you want strict isolation, Redwood Private (VPC) is the cleanest from an audit/compliance standpoint. For a faster start, Dedicated in EU region with Egress controls can often meet the requirement if you manage encryption/KMS keys.

2) Perf gating & canary plan:
   - We'll run a 72-hour perf harness: ramp to 120 QPS sustained, include burst windows to 700 QPS, and exercise 80 concurrent streaming sessions.
   - We'll capture token-level latency (model + network) and end-to-end p95.

3) Clarifying data points needed (can you share these if available):
   - Average and 95th percentile request size in tokens (you provided estimates — can you confirm sample CSV with 200 rows of representative requests?).
   - Are streams WebSocket-based or long-poll? (WebSocket preferred for realistic concurrency checks).

4) Network & security:
   - We'll need the egress ranges (received), and also any inbound firewall rules for our perf harness IPs (we'll propose IPs once POC window dates are confirmed).

5) Test artifacts:
   - I'll attach a short perf test plan for your review (redwood-perf-test-plan-20270504.docx). If that looks good we can lock dates.

If these are green, next step is to schedule the perf window and get your team to approve the test dates. Lauren — can you share a calendar link for a 30-min alignment?

Thanks,

Aditya Rao
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
